items.title: Chinese-linked hackers use AI tool Artex to automate attacks on ConnectWise and Korean banks
items.summary: A Chinese-linked hacking group used the AI-based tool 'Artex' to automate cyberattacks targeting hundreds of organizations worldwide, including US IT firm ConnectWise and over 16 Korean financial institutions. The AI system enabled rapid, autonomous data breaches and unauthorized access, resulting in significant privacy and security harms.

items.title: Meta's AI Moderation Wrongfully Removes Election Posts by Brazilian Newspaper
items.summary: Meta's AI-driven content moderation system removed at least 31 legitimate election-related posts by the newspaper O Estado de S. Paulo from Facebook and Instagram during Brazil's elections. The removals, attributed to AI misuse, led the newspaper to seek legal intervention to prevent further wrongful censorship and demand human review of future moderation actions.

items.title: Unauthorized AI Membership Sales Lead to Data Breaches and Fraud Risks in China
items.summary: Multiple Chinese AI platforms, including Doubao, DeepSeek, and Kimi, have seen their paid memberships and API keys illicitly sold or rented on secondary markets. This misuse exposes users to privacy breaches, data theft, financial losses, and legal violations, as unauthorized access allows third parties to view and potentially sell user data.

items.title: Barclays to cut around 5,000 jobs, citing AI-driven efficiency
items.summary: Barclays bank announced plans to cut around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of 2026. The reductions are primarily due to increased use of AI for operational efficiency, with 60% affecting support functions and developers. The move results in significant economic harm to affected employees.

items.title: London Police Deploy Live Facial Recognition at Chelsea-Tottenham Match
items.summary: The Metropolitan Police will deploy live facial recognition technology around Stamford Bridge during the Chelsea vs. Tottenham football match in London. The AI system will scan crowds to identify individuals on watchlists, raising concerns about privacy and potential human rights violations due to mass surveillance at public events.

items.title: South Korean man referred for prosecution over AI smart glasses used to cheat on national exam
items.summary: A 20-year-old man in South Korea was sent to prosecution for using AI-enabled smart glasses linked to a smartphone app to cheat during a national technical qualification exam. The incident highlights growing concerns over AI misuse in exams, with several similar cases recently reported.

items.title: AI-assisted attacks on Indian bank APIs lead to breaches and unauthorized transfers; RBI tightens rules
items.summary: Hackers have used sophisticated AI tools to exploit vulnerabilities in Indian banks' API systems, leading to data breaches and unauthorized fund transfers. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has responded by mandating stricter cybersecurity measures and compliance checks to address these AI-related risks and protect financial institutions and customers.

items.title: Greek Study Links TikTok's AI Algorithms to Addiction and Mental Health Issues in Young People
items.summary: A University of Athens study found that nearly half of Greeks under 30 show addiction symptoms to TikTok, an AI-driven platform. Excessive use, averaging 2.3 hours daily, is linked to increased anxiety, depression, and sleep problems, highlighting the mental health impact of AI-powered recommendation systems.

items.title: IMF and OECD Warn AI Adoption May Widen Global Economic Inequality
items.summary: Officials from the IMF and OECD warn that AI adoption is leading to significant layoffs and job displacement, especially among young and entry-level workers. Poorer countries and smaller businesses face challenges accessing AI, risking increased economic inequality and social harm as AI automates tasks and boosts productivity.

items.title: Study finds Gemini and GPT-4o paired with smart glasses can answer most SAT questions
items.summary: Research by German scientists demonstrated that AI models like Google's Gemini and OpenAI's GPT-4o, when paired with smart glasses, can solve over 80% of SAT questions, even under image distortion. Actual incidents of exam cheating using AI-enabled smart glasses have been detected, raising concerns about academic integrity and prompting stricter monitoring.

items.title: AI-generated image falsely showing singer Vasilis Papakonstantinou in hospital spreads in Greece
items.summary: An AI-generated deepfake image falsely depicting singer Vasilis Papakonstantinou in a hospital was widely circulated online, causing emotional distress, reputational harm, and public confusion. Actress Eleni Rantou publicly condemned the misuse of AI for spreading false and offensive content, highlighting the incident's impact on individuals and the community.

items.title: Goldman Sachs Forecasts AI Could Displace Up to 9% of U.S. Workers
items.summary: Goldman Sachs research, led by economist Joseph Briggs, estimates that artificial intelligence could displace up to 9% of U.S. workers—about 15 million people—over a decade. The analysis highlights potential job losses and slower hiring due to AI-driven productivity gains, with impacts likely intensifying during economic downturns.

items.title: 19-year-old arrested in Bulgaria over alleged AI-assisted cyberattacks on media and state institutions
items.summary: A 19-year-old, Mariyan Parushev, was arrested in Bulgaria for allegedly using artificial intelligence to conduct large-scale cyberattacks against national media and state institutions. The attacks involved data theft and trading stolen information via Telegram, with payments in cryptocurrency. The court ordered his detention due to the severity of the offenses.

items.title: Wenjie M9 with AI driving systems crashes and catches fire in Shaanxi, killing driver
items.summary: A Wenjie M9 vehicle, equipped with AI-based driving and safety systems, crashed and caught fire in Shaanxi, China, resulting in the driver's death. The incident raised public concerns about the effectiveness of the car's AI safety features, data transparency, and the rapid post-collision fire, prompting scrutiny of AI system reliability in vehicles.

items.title: AI Accelerates Youth Radicalisation in Australia, Authorities Warn
items.summary: Australian authorities, including the Federal Police and security agencies, report that AI-driven online platforms are rapidly accelerating the radicalisation and manipulation of vulnerable youth. This has led to increased youth crime, psychological harm, and extremist acts, with radicalisation now occurring in days rather than months or years.

items.title: Exin Therapeutics AI agent selects gene therapy and guides robotic brain injection in live mouse
items.summary: Exin Therapeutics, a San Francisco biotech startup, used an AI agent to autonomously select a gene therapy and guide a robotic injector into a live mouse's brain. The AI controlled treatment choice and injection parameters, with human supervision and safety measures in place. No harm was reported, but the procedure posed inherent risks.

items.title: Kim Jong-un announces priority on AI integration in North Korean military drones
items.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un announced the prioritization of artificial intelligence integration into unmanned weapon systems and military drones to modernize the country's armed forces. The initiative, revealed at a military exhibition, aims for "absolute superiority" in drone technology, raising concerns about future AI-enabled military risks.

items.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain attack steals credentials via PyPI and Docker images
items.summary: A supply chain attack compromised the LiteLLM AI gateway (version 1.107.0), distributing malware via PyPI and Docker images. The malicious code stole cloud, AI, and SSH credentials and enabled remote code execution. Attackers also hijacked exposed LiteLLM and Ollama servers due to lack of authentication, leading to unauthorized access and further attacks.

items.title: Australian class action alleges Meta's Facebook and Instagram algorithms harmed minors
items.summary: Eight individuals in Australia filed a class action lawsuit against Meta, alleging that Facebook and Instagram's AI-driven algorithms fostered addictive behaviors and exposed minors to harmful content. The case highlights claims that the platforms' algorithmic design directly harmed children's health and well-being, prompting legal and regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Hackers reportedly used AI to find vulnerabilities and launder $6.3 billion stolen from Binance
items.summary: Hackers used artificial intelligence to automate and obscure laundering of $6.3 billion stolen from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. AI tools enabled rapid discovery of vulnerabilities and complex transaction patterns, making detection difficult. The incident caused major financial losses and disrupted crypto markets.
